blocks.title: Introduction
blocks.content: Let $F$ be a field of characteristic zero and $t\in F$. Recently P. Deligne introduced the tensor category $\underline{\operatorname{Re}}\!\operatorname{p}(S_t)$ which in a certain precise sense interpolates the categories $\operatorname{Rep}(S_d)$ of $F-$linear representations of the symmetric groups $S_d$, see [@Del07]. blocks.title: Terminology and notation conventions
blocks.content:
[]{#notation label="notation"} Let $F$ be a field. A *tensor category* is an $F$-linear[^1] category $\mathcal{T}$ along with an $F$-linear bifunctor $\otimes:\mathcal{T}\times\mathcal{T}\to\mathcal{T}$ and associativity, commutativity, and unit constraints satisfying the triangle, pentagon, and hexagon axioms (see [@MR1797619]). Moreover, we require our tensor categories to be rigid with $\text{End}_\mathcal{T}({\bf 1})=F$.

To do so, consider the element a := εε′ + (1 −ε)(1 −ε′) ∈A. If ¯ε = ε′, then ¯a = ¯1. Hence a is a unit in A (see Lemma A.1). Moreover, εa = εε′ = aε′ so that ε = aε′a−1. □

blocks.title: Appendix A. On lifting idempotents
blocks.content:
As we were unable to ﬁnd an appropriate reference, in this appendix we give
standard proofs of well-known results on lifting idempotents. Assume F is a ﬁeld,
u is an indeterminate, and A is a free F[[u]]-algebra of ﬁnite rank. Finally, for
a ∈A, let ¯a denote the image of a under the quotient map A →A/Au. In this
appendix we will show that any idempotent in the F-algebra A/Au can be lifted
to an idempotent in A. First, we need the following lemma.
Lemma A.1. a is a unit in A if and only if ¯a is a unit in A/Au.
Proof. If a is a unit in A, then clearly ¯a is a unit in A/Au with ¯a−1 = a−1. Now

2. Given an idempotent e ∈A/Au, there exists an idempotent ε ∈A such that ¯ε = e (we say ε is a lift of e). Moreover, if two idempotents are conjugate in A/Au, then their lifts are conjugate in A. ‡The equations in (6.14) are only deﬁned when m is suﬃciently large. JONATHAN COMES AND VICTOR OSTRIK
